prompt_md: Car A goes from 10 to 15 km per litre. Car B now does 20 km per litre. To save as much fuel per km as car A did, what must car B's new km per litre be?
prompt_short: A goes from 10 to 15 km/L. B at 20 km/L must reach what to save as much?
hint_md: Compare litres per km, not km per litre.
explain_intuition_md: Fuel used is litres per km, the flip of km per litre. Car A drops from 1/10 to 1/15 of a litre per km, and matching that saving takes car B much further than a 50% boost.
